title: Activity, Task, Package, and Window Manager Boundaries Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies activity, task, package, and window manager boundaries?
options: Assign package, task, process, and window facts to their distinct authorities and trace the tokens and Binder calls connecting them.
Assume one activity equals one window forever
questions.answer: Assign package, task, process, and window facts to their distinct authorities and trace the tokens and Binder calls connecting them.
questions.explanation: This answer keeps the ownership boundaries distinct and requires version-matched evidence, failure testing, compatibility, and operational follow-through.

questions.prompt: ActivityTaskManager owns the installed signature and permission metadata used for intent resolution.
questions.explanation: Equating an activity task with a Linux process fails because tasks can outlive processes and one process can host components participating in different task states.

questions.prompt: Which service boundary owns installed component and signature metadata?
questions.answer: PackageManager; task, process, and window services consume that information for their own responsibilities.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the mechanism and owner that make the explanation causal rather than a memorised sequence.
